product.idguide: NOT FOUND in the public documentation read on 8 November 2026.
product.additional:
Illustrative example for the Cyber Manual Movement, built by the Value Chain Risk Institute with the CRA Manual Builder from public documentation read on 8 November 2026. It is NOT the manufacturer's manual and makes no claim about CRA conformity. Gaps are marked NOT FOUND rather than filled in.
Hardware manufactured by Banana Pi in collaboration with the OpenWrt project; the firmware is the OpenWrt project's. Which party is the CRA manufacturer is left to the working group. The OpenWrt project is not a legal person, so it is not listed as an open-source software steward (reply on the openwrt-adm list, 10 November 2026).
Flash sizes conflict between sources: the OpenWrt wiki (edited 23 Oct 2026) says 256 MiB NAND and 16 MiB NOR; the Software Freedom Conservancy page says 128 MiB NAND and 4 MiB NOR. This example uses the wiki figures.
Version 0.2, 11 November 2026: corrected and completed from a reply on the openwrt-adm mailing list (10 November 2026). The fact sheet beside this file quotes it.

er1.2b: NOT MET BY DEFAULT: after a fresh installation or upgrade no root password is set (OpenWrt security page). The owner must set one before use; see chapter 3.2.
er1.2g:
The product only processes the following data:
Network traffic routed between WAN, LAN and Wi-Fi
Configuration, including Wi-Fi keys and the root password
er1.2l: NOT FOUND in the public documentation read on 8 November 2026.

er2.v-test: The OpenWrt project runs uscan weekly (package versions against upstream, and CVEs by CPE) and Coverity Scan weekly on OpenWrt-developed components.
er2.v-sbom: NOT FOUND in the public documentation read on 8 November 2026.
er2.v-pub: Advisories are published at openwrt.org/docs/guide-developer/security. They cover OpenWrt-maintained components only, not upstream components such as the Linux kernel or OpenSSL.
er2.v-cvd: Report confidentially to contact@openwrt.org. The mailbox is not always monitored; if there is no answer, send a brief note without exploit details to openwrt-adm@lists.openwrt.org.

pc.title: 256 MiB SPI NAND (normal boot: bootloader, kernel, root file system)
16 MiB SPI NOR (recovery system, write-protect jumper)
OpenWrt firmware with the LuCI web interface

pi.title: 2.5 Gbit Ethernet (WAN by default; PoE powered device, 802.3af/at)
Front button and rear Reset button

pp.proto: USB mass storage (FAT32) read by the bootloader
pp.fc: FC04 Recover the firmware; FC05 Install security updates

pp.proto: Request to the Attended Sysupgrade server

sp.title: Write-protected recovery system
sp.desc: A stripped-down recovery system lives in SPI NOR, protected by the NOR WP jumper in its factory default position. With the boot switch on NOR, it re-flashes the whole NAND from a USB drive, even if the NAND bootloader or Trusted Firmware-A is broken.

sp.title: Security fixes backported to supported releases
sp.desc: The OpenWrt project backports security fixes for its core components to supported releases. Package fixes reach users in about two days through the build bots; kernel and kernel-module fixes need a new minor release.

sp.title: Compiler hardening by default
sp.desc: Packages are built with format-security checks, stack protector (regular), FORTIFY_SOURCE=1, full RELRO and PIE for network-exposed binaries; the kernel has seccomp enabled. SELinux is not enabled.

sp.title: Open source with reproducibility checks
sp.desc: The firmware source is public and copyleft-compliant from the start. The reproducible-builds project checks that OpenWrt master builds reproducibly.

cc.title: Upstream network
cc.desc: The modem or ISP network connected to the 2.5 Gbit WAN port.

cc.title: Wired LAN devices
cc.desc: Computers and devices connected to the 1 Gbit LAN port or a switch behind it.

cc.title: Administration computer
cc.desc: A computer with a browser (LuCI) or SSH client used to configure the router.

cc.title: OpenWrt download and build servers
cc.desc: Release download pages, the Firmware Selector and the Attended Sysupgrade server.

cc.title: USB drive
cc.desc: A FAT32 drive holding a sysupgrade or recovery image.

cc.title: Recovery host
cc.desc: A computer with a serial terminal and, for NOR re-flashing, a TFTP server at 192.168.11.23.

cp.title: Owner / administrator
cp.desc: The person who sets up and maintains the router.

cp.title: Network users
cp.desc: People whose devices use the network.

cp.title: Recovery technician
cp.desc: A person re-flashing NAND or NOR using the recovery procedures.

cz.title: Home network
cz.desc: LAN and Wi-Fi under the owner's control

cz.title: Physical location
cz.desc: The room where the router is installed

fc.title: Route and filter traffic
fc.desc: Forward traffic between the WAN port, the LAN port and Wi-Fi.
fc.rfu: Use with the LAN and WAN ports swapped; one user reported this out of the box.

fc.title: Provide Wi-Fi access
fc.rfu: Operation without setting the country code.

fc.title: Administer the router
fc.desc: Configuration through LuCI at http://192.168.1.1 or SSH as root.
fc.rfu: Administration from outside the home network.

fc.title: Recover the firmware
fc.desc: NAND initramfs recovery (front button), NOR full recovery (boot switch on NOR, USB drive), and NOR re-flashing over UART and TFTP.

fc.title: Install security updates
fc.desc: User-initiated upgrade through LuCI Attended Sysupgrade, owut on the command line, the web Firmware Selector, or a USB drive read by the bootloader.
fc.rfu: Installing SNAPSHOT builds instead of a release.

cu.title: Set a strong root password before use
cu.desc: Set it in LuCI (System > Administration > Router Password) or with passwd, before connecting other devices or enabling Wi-Fi.

cu.title: Confirm the WAN and LAN ports
cu.desc: Connect the upstream network to the 2.5 Gbit port and check in LuCI that it is the WAN interface before going online.

cu.title: Run a supported release
cu.desc: Use a release with Supported or Security Maintenance status (25.12 as of 8 November 2026) and upgrade before it reaches End of Life.

cu.title: Set the country code and use WPA2 or WPA3
cu.desc: Set the Wi-Fi country code first, then protect every SSID with WPA2 or WPA3.

cu.title: No administration from the internet
cu.desc: Keep LuCI and SSH reachable from the home network only.

cu.title: Limit password guessing
cu.desc: LuCI has no built-in brute-force protection. Restrict who can reach it, or install a tool such as fail2ban.

cu.title: Control physical access
cu.desc: The serial console has no password prompt unless one is enabled, and the buttons and boot switch allow re-flashing. Keep the device where only trusted people can reach it.

cu.affected: CC05 OpenWrt download and build servers
cu.title: Use only official images
cu.desc: Obtain images only from the OpenWrt download pages, the Firmware Selector or Attended Sysupgrade.

cu.title: Keep the NOR write protection
cu.desc: Leave the NOR WP jumper in its factory position; when re-flashing NOR, unlock it from the boot menu, then lock it again (menu item 7) and remove the jumper.

ri.title: No root password
ri.desc: The owner never sets a root password.
ri.risk: Anyone on the LAN or Wi-Fi can log in as root through LuCI or SSH and take full control.

ri.title: Ports swapped
ri.desc: The upstream network is plugged into the LAN port.
ri.risk: The administration interfaces face the upstream network.

ri.title: End-of-life release
ri.desc: The router stays on a release past End of Life (24.10 reached it in September 2026).
ri.risk: New vulnerabilities, even severe ones, are no longer fixed.

ri.title: Open or misconfigured Wi-Fi
ri.desc: An SSID runs without WPA2 or WPA3, or without the correct country code.
ri.risk: Strangers can join the network; operation may break radio rules.

ri.title: Administration exposed to the internet
ri.desc: LuCI or SSH is opened to the WAN side.
ri.risk: Attackers on the internet can attempt to log in or exploit the interface.

ri.title: Password guessing
ri.desc: LuCI is reachable by many devices and nothing limits login attempts.
ri.risk: A weak password can be guessed.

ri.title: Unattended physical access
ri.desc: Untrusted people can reach the device.
ri.risk: Console access or re-flashing gives full control.

ri.title: Image from an unofficial source
ri.desc: A firmware image is taken from a forum, a mirror or a seller.

ri.title: NOR left unlocked
ri.desc: NOR is not locked again after re-flashing.
ri.risk: The recovery system can be overwritten, so the failsafe no longer protects the device.

commissioning:
Set the NAND/NOR switch to NAND (up).
Connect a computer to the 1 Gbit port (LAN by default) and power the device by USB-C or PoE on the 2.5 Gbit port.
Open http://192.168.1.1 and log in as root with an empty password, then set a strong root password immediately.
Set the Wi-Fi country code before enabling Wi-Fi.
Check that a supported release is installed and upgrade if not.

updates.note: Updates are user-initiated: LuCI System > Attended Sysupgrade, owut upgrade on the command line, the web Firmware Selector, or a USB drive read by the bootloader (hold Reset at power-on). Package fixes can arrive in about two days; kernel fixes need a new minor release image.
updates.disableAuto: The product does not install updates automatically.
updates.end: Per OpenWrt release, not per device: 25.12 is Supported with end of life to be announced. A release reaches End of Life one year after its initial release or six months after the next major release, whichever is later. No hardware support period is published: the release policy covers OpenWrt software releases, and the project does not declare one for hardware it does not sell (reply on the openwrt-adm list, 10 November 2026).

decommission:
Use NOR recovery to factory re-flash the entire NAND, which removes the configuration, Wi-Fi keys and passwords.
Remove any USB drive or NVMe SSD; they keep their data.
